chunks: And from them, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Barqi Muhammad ibn Khald, from 'Abd al-'Azim ibn 'Abdillah al-Hasani, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hakam al-Nakha'i, from Kathir ibn Shihab al-Harithi, who said:
While we were sitting with the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) in al-Rahbah, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered. He smiled a smile until his front teeth became visible.
Then he said: Indeed, Allah mentioned a people and said, 'Nor did the heavens weep over them, nor the earth, nor were they granted respite.'
And by He who split the grain and created the living beings, this one will surely be killed, and the heavens and the earth will weep over him.

key_terms.الرَّحَبَة: A public square or open area in Kufa
key_terms.بَرَأَ النَّسَمَة: He who created the living being/soul
key_terms.فَلَقَ الْحَبَّةَ: He who split the grain (a reference to Quran 6:95, describing Allah's creative power)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the heavens weeping for Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this renowned narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Ali’s (a.s.) visible joy upon seeing Imam Husayn (a.s.) is interpreted by Shia scholars as a glad tiding of his high status and the cosmic significance of his martyrdom. By contrasting the unwept-for people of the Quran with Husayn, the Imam establishes a unique metaphysical reality where the heavens and earth actively mourn his death, elevating his sacrifice beyond mere historical event to a universal spiritual phenomenon.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 16. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain both narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid Al-Barqi, from ‘Abdil ‘Aďīm ibn ‘Abdillāh Al-Ḥasani, from Ḥasan ibn Ḥakam Al-Nakha’i, from Kuthayr ibn Shihāb Al-Ḥārithi, who said:

(One day) while we were sitting with the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) in Ruḥbah, Ḥusain (a.s.) entered. (When the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) saw him), he smiled in a way that one could see his teeth.

Then he (the Commander of the Believers (a.s.)) said: Allāh has mentioned some people in the Qur’an by saying, “Neither did the heavens weep over them, nor the earth, nor were they granted respite” [44:29].
I swear to He, who split the grain and created the living beings, that he (Ḥusain (a.s.)) will be killed and the heavens and the earth will weep over him.
